title: Phase 1 — baseline green + safe cuts
description:
## Goal

CI green on all three OSes, ~2.5k LOC of off-vision surface gone, no behaviour a user depends on changes. Every deletion here is independently revertable and is gated on the three baseline repairs being green first.

## Why this phase exists first

The tree is red in three places today and two of the three are disk-touching. Nothing else in the plan can be verified while `cargo test` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` fail, so this phase is a hard blocker for all four that follow. It also removes the surfaces the vision explicitly cut, which shrinks every later diff.

## Scope

- Three baseline repairs (see child beads) — one is a data-loss-adjacent bug, one is a live production crash.
- Nine cut-list items: `ro-dep-update`, `ro fork`, `ro self-update`, `ro robot-docs`, TOON + the `ro-output` crate, `ro import`, the health *display*, `ro review`, and the already-dead helpers.
- One migration, `V4_DROP_PLANS`, dropping the `plans` table and the `repos.default_branch` column.
- `ro schema` lands in the SAME commit that deletes `generate_robot_docs`.

## Explicitly NOT cut in this phase

- `ro sweep commit-sweep` stays — it is the only working fleet-commit path until `ro ship` ships in Phase 5. The `Bucket` classifier is deleted in Phase 4, atomically with the namespace cut.
- `ro sync --parallel/-j`, `--resume`, `--timeout`, `--quiet`, `--verbose` flags stay until Phase 5, but **stop advertising them** in README/FEATURES now. A silently-accepted no-op flag is worse than an error.

## Done looks like

Four modules, ten commands in three tiers, five migrations (V1-V4 plus the new V5), `ro schema` live, no agent-facing surface missing. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` all green on Windows, macOS, and Linux. `ro remove` and `ro prune` still work against a **v3** database, proving the V4 migration path. `ro sweep commit-sweep --all` still works, proving nothing it depends on was cut.

title: Fix the Windows orphan-detection separator bug
description:
## The bug

`crates/ro-sync/src/manage.rs:286-293` (`resolve_local_path`) builds stored paths with `format!("{}/{}/{}", projects_dir.display(), owner, name)` — **forward slashes on Windows**. `crates/ro-sync/src/prune.rs:149` walks with `PathBuf::join` — **backslashes** — and compares them as raw `String`s.

On Windows **every tracked repo is reported as an orphan**. Two tests are red right now for this reason: `prune::tests::find_orphans_returns_empty_when_all_tracked` and `prune::tests::find_orphans_reports_untracked_working_copies`.

## Accurate framing of the harm

`handle_orphans` with `Delete` is gated at `crates/ro/src/main.rs:803-812` (requires `--non-interactive` or a TTY) and then `confirm()` returns false on a non-TTY. The realistic harm is **a TTY user being shown a list that wrongly contains their own managed repos and typing `y`** — not silent deletion. Still fix it first: the failure mode is data loss and the blast radius is the entire registry.

## The fix has TWO halves and both are required

1. **`resolve_local_path` uses `PathBuf::join`.** This fixes rows written *after* the change.
2. **The comparison side canonicalizes-with-fallback.** This is the part that rescues every **already-persisted** forward-slash `local_path` in existing `state.db` files.

**Without half 2, the fix converts a wrong list into every existing user's repos becoming orphans.** This is an acceptance criterion, not a regression test — a test that only exercises freshly-written rows will pass while shipping the worse bug.

## Tests

- Mixed-separator regression: a tracked repo with a forward-slash stored path is NOT reported as an orphan.
- A repo stored with `PathBuf::join` separators is not reported.
- Both red tests go green.
acceptance_criteria: Both prune tests green on Windows. Mixed-separator regression test present and passing. resolve_local_path uses PathBuf::join AND the comparison side canonicalizes.
close_reason: Both halves landed: resolve_local_path (manage.rs:267) uses PathBuf::join, and prune.rs compares via paths_equivalent with canonicalize-with-fallback so pre-existing forward-slash rows in a live state.db are not reported as orphans. Mixed-separator regression test at prune.rs:554.

title: Cut the health display, KEEP the health scorer
description:
## The distinction that makes this bead right

A 0-100 score that nobody acts on is noise. A 0-100 score that narrows a twenty-repo fleet to the repos that need a human is a selector. **Cut the display, keep the computation.**

An earlier revision of the plan cut both, and was wrong: `--filter health:<N>` is the one way to say "only the repos that actually need attention" across a fleet, and the scorer already exists and already has seven tests.

## What goes

- `Commands::Health` and its handler arm
- The `HealthClass` **display** enum
- The health entries in the (now-deleted) robot-docs literals

## What STAYS — do not delete these

- **`crates/ro-state/src/queries.rs` in full** (275 LOC, 7 tests: `HealthClass`, `HealthSnapshot`, `score_repo_health`, `latest_health`, `score_all_health`, `row_to_health`)
- **`pub mod queries;`** in `ro-state/src/lib.rs`
- **The `health:<N>` branch in `resolve_multi_repo_targets`** so `--filter health:<N>` keeps working on `ro sync`
- `HealthClass`'s `Debug`/`Serialize` derives — the filter now consumes it. Delete **only** the `Display` impl, and only if it exists to feed the removed table output.

## Test

`ro sync --filter health:critical` selects a subset; `--filter health:99` selects none, using **real `repo_health_snapshots` rows** — not a substring match. And `ro list --format text` and `--format json` contain **no** `Health`/`health` key anywhere in their output. The display/compute split is the contract; assert both halves.

Today `--filter tag:orch` matches any repo whose owner or name contains "orch" — a fake selector. Do not reproduce that here.
acceptance_criteria: ro health command gone. ro-state/src/queries.rs intact with all 7 tests. --filter health:<N> selects on real snapshot rows. No health key in ro list output.
close_reason: Commands::Health, its handler and the display enum are gone (5014d61), and the orphaned section markers plus the dangling 'Show health score for repos' doc comment have now been removed from main.rs. The scorer survives as the plan requires: ro-state/src/queries.rs keeps HealthClass, HealthSnapshot, score_repo_health, latest_health and score_all_health (17 tests), and main.rs:463 still honours the health:<N> filter.

title: Delete ro review, add V4_DROP_PLANS, fix the delete_repo_cascade landmine
description:
## What

- Delete `crates/ro-review/` (541 LOC, 13 tests), `Commands::Review`, the `ReviewCommands` enum, `fn parse_risk`, its handler arm, `AutoApproveLevel`, `ReviewConfig`, the matching `ro-config/src/validate.rs:50-61` review blocks, the `[review]` block in `DEFAULT_CONFIG_TOML`, and the `ro-config/src/paths.rs` test assertion on `review`.

**Good news:** `ro-review::apply_plan` (`apply.rs:22-45`) only runs `UPDATE plans SET status='applied'` — `ro review apply` **never touched a repo**. Deletion carries zero behavioural or data-loss risk.

**Do NOT confuse** `ro_sweep::agent::SweepSummary.plan_created: bool` (in-memory, live, `main.rs:1113`) and `ro_output::ndjson::NdjsonEvent::plan_created` with the `plans` **table**. They are unrelated to ro-review.

## The migration — exactly two statements

```sql
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS plans;
ALTER TABLE repos DROP COLUMN default_branch;
```

**`repo_health_snapshots` is NOT dropped** — the health scorer survives as the `--filter health:` selector — so the migration does not touch the health FK chain at all.

**Do NOT edit `V1_INITIAL_SCHEMA`.** `migrate::run` records applied versions in `_meta.version` and only applies migrations with `version > current`, so a V1 edit never reaches an already-initialized database.

The `ALTER TABLE` is SQLite 3.35+ (2021). The workspace pins `rusqlite` with `bundled` — **check the bundled version rather than assuming**.

## THE HIGHEST-RISK ITEM IN THE WHOLE MIGRATION

`crates/ro-sync/src/manage.rs` hard-codes table names as **raw string literals**:
- `NULLABLE_FK_TABLES` contains `"plans"` — **remove it**
- `CHILD_TABLES` contains `"repo_health_snapshots"` — **this entry STAYS**

Getting this backwards leaves `cargo check`, `cargo clippy`, **and** `cargo test` **all green**, then breaks `ro remove` at runtime with a SQLite no-such-table error. **It is invisible to every static check.**

## default_branch has readers that must be rewritten, not just a column to drop

The rebase base inside `ro push` and the empty-repo base inference both read it today. Both move to `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` — one git command, correct for any clone. The `--default-branch` flag is deleted with the column.

**Grep for the name before running the migration.** A `SELECT` left behind is a runtime failure on an upgraded database, and the migration itself will succeed.

## Tests

- The upgraded-database test: open a `state.db` created by the **pre-V4** binary, apply V4, then run `ro remove` and `ro prune` against it. This is the **only** test that catches a stale `SELECT` — a freshly-built test database has the column absent and the reader compiles fine.
- `remove_clears_dependent_rows` (`manage.rs:437`) loses **only** its `plans` assertions; the `repo_health_snapshots` ones stay.
- `score_repo_health` calls at `ro-sync/prune.rs:369,381` are untouched — health scoring is still live.
acceptance_criteria: ro-review deleted. V4 has exactly the two statements. manage.rs NULLABLE_FK_TABLES has no "plans"; CHILD_TABLES still has "repo_health_snapshots". A pre-V4 database upgrades and ro remove / ro prune work against it. --filter health:<N> still selects.
close_reason: ro-review crate, Commands::Review, ReviewCommands, parse_risk and the handler deleted in 5014d61; V4_DROP_PLANS appended in bdffbbc. The landmine is defused: NULLABLE_FK_TABLES is now ["jobs"] with a comment naming the trap, CHILD_TABLES still holds repo_health_snapshots, and the migration body is exactly the two statements the plan specifies. The v3_database_upgrades_to_v4 test proves the upgrade path on a populated database.

title: Delete dead helpers and edit the four lib.rs files in the same commits
description:

## The four lib.rs edits

2. `schema.rs::round_trip_through_toml` (line 280, asserts `parsed.jobs.max_attempts`)

- After `policy_check.rs` goes, `ro-config` and `serde_yaml` also become dead in `ro-sweep/Cargo.toml`. **Neither was on the original list.**
- `ro-output` must be removed from **four** places: root members, root `[workspace.dependencies]`, `crates/ro/Cargo.toml`, and `crates/ro-sweep/Cargo.toml`.

- Workspace: `comfy_table`, `console`, `sha2`, `owo_colors`
- Per-crate: `ro-git{tokio, serde_json, ro-core, regex}`, `ro-sweep{ro-core, ro-jobs, ro-output, tokio, comfy-table, ro-config, serde_yaml}`, `ro-sync{tokio, indicatif, console}`, `ro-github{reqwest, time}`, and `ro-config`'s unused `ro-core`

Its `[advisories] ignore` list references `RUSTSEC-2024-0436` (via `rmcp`, a crate deleted in commit `5fdece9`) and `RUSTSEC-2025-0119` (via `indicatif`, which this phase removes from `ro-sync`). `.github/workflows/audit.yml` mirrors the same ignores and runs `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources` on **every push**.

Stale ignores are at best noise and at worst a hard failure depending on cargo-deny version. **Clean both files.**

## Correct two wrong comments in files this phase touches

- `ro-output/src/lib.rs:11` says TOON is "retained for `ru` compatibility" and the crate description lists all four renderers.

description:

`crates/ro-sync/src/prune.rs:135` — `if let Ok(p) = r` where only the `Ok` variant of the iterator element is used. Clippy suggests `.flatten()`.

## Why it is P1 and not a nit

title: Fix the ro import --stars production panic, then record the diagnosis
description:
## This is a live production crash, not test hygiene

`crates/ro-github/src/import.rs:29` calls `crate::auth::build_client` (which calls `Octocrab::builder().build()`) **before** `tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()` on line 31. `Octocrab::builder().build()` panics with `there is no reactor running` outside a runtime.

**So `ro import --stars` panics on any machine where a token is discoverable.** It passes on CI only because `gh` is off `PATH` there, which is exactly why it went unnoticed.

## The fix

- Move `bail!("no import source specified")` **before** the client is constructed.
- Build the client **inside** `rt.block_on`.

**Adding `#[tokio::test]` does NOT fix it** — `Runtime::new()` inside a runtime panics with `cannot start a runtime from within a runtime`. This is the trap: the obvious fix makes it worse.

## Why fix it at all if the file is being deleted

The file is cut in a sibling bead (`cut-ro-import`), and the cut does not need this fixed. Fix it **first anyway**, so the diagnosis is recorded in git history. A crash that existed in a released binary deserves a commit that says what it was and why it went unnoticed, not a silent file deletion.

## Test

`ro-github::import::tests::fetch_without_source_errors` must pass **with `gh` on PATH** — that is the condition under which it fails today and the condition CI never exercised. Assert both: `gh` present (the crash case) and absent (the current CI case).
acceptance_criteria: The test passes with gh on PATH. No Octocrab::builder() call occurs outside a runtime. Diagnosis recorded in the commit message.
close_reason: Diagnosed and fixed in 004801e (client build moved inside rt.block_on, bail moved before client construction), then the file was cut in 3d7698c. ro-github/src/import.rs no longer exists.

title: Replace ro robot-docs with a clap-derived ro schema
description:
## Two changes, ONE commit

1. **Delete** `Commands::RobotDocs` and `fn generate_robot_docs` (`crates/ro/src/main.rs:487-551`, 65 lines of hand-written `json!` literals) plus its dispatch arm.
2. **Add** `ro schema`, built from `clap::CommandFactory` — already a dependency, roughly 30 lines serializing the live command tree.

## Why the generator has to die

It has **already drifted** from the clap tree in four places:
- `commands` omits `commit-sweep` from the sweep subcommands
- `prune` omits `--orphans/--archive/--delete`
- `formats` lists only text/json, contradicting FEATURES.md's toon section
- `quickstart` still recommends `ro health`

`FEATURES.md:236-239` promises an `all` topic that does not exist. A hand-maintained mirror of a clap tree is a thing that is wrong the moment it is written.

## Why they must be atomic

The vision asks for "a single JSON API/schema surface for agents" as the **replacement**. A four-phase absence of the machine-readable surface, while six other surfaces change, is the worst possible window for anything that drives ro programmatically. Deleting the old one and landing the new one in the same commit means no gap.

## Compatibility break — state it in the release notes

`ro schema` is a **live clap-tree dump**, a genuinely different artifact from the hand-written JSON summary. Any agent parsing `ro robot-docs commands` **breaks**. This goes in the release note, not just the commit message — it is a behavioural change visible to exactly the audience most likely to have automated around it.

## Test

`ro schema` output, parsed, contains every command and flag the clap tree actually has. A test that compares the schema's command list against `Cli::command()` would be circular; assert against a hand-written list of the ten target commands instead, so a newly added command that forgets the schema fails the test.
acceptance_criteria: ro schema exists and emits a clap-derived tree. ro robot-docs is gone. No window where neither exists. Release note names the compatibility break.
close_reason: generate_robot_docs deleted and ro schema added from clap::CommandFactory in a29e162. crates/ro/tests/cli_schema.rs (6 tests) pins the shape, including that it documents no removed command.

title: Cut TOON and delete the ro-output crate, moving the live NDJSON surface
description:
## What goes

- `OutputFormat::Toon` (`main.rs:26`), `fn print_toon` (`main.rs:30-35`), and 6 dispatch arms (`main.rs:663, 758, 790, 896, 1322, 1419-1425`).
- `ro_output::text::write_toon` + `uniform_object_keys` (`text.rs:29-72`) and 4 tests.
- The `Toon` arms in `ro-output/src/lib.rs` (`OutputFormat`, `Display`, `parse_output_format`, `render`).

## Why the WHOLE crate goes, not just the format

`ro_output::{OutputFormat, parse_output_format, render}` have **zero external callers** — `write_value` is reached only from inside the dead `render()` at `ro-output/src/lib.rs:68`. Cutting toon orphans the entire `ro_output::text` module, and what remains is a crate the binary barely uses.

## What MOVES, and where — this is the part that is easy to get wrong

The **8 live `NdjsonEvent` constructors** are called at `main.rs:1087, 1099, 1107, 1124, 1130, 1116, 1145, 1152` inside the `sweep agent` handler, and `text::write_toon` at `main.rs:32`.

Under the new architecture the orchestrator lives in the `ro` binary, so **both move into the binary**: the `NdjsonEvent { kind, ts, #[serde(flatten)] payload }` envelope kept **verbatim** into `crates/ro/src/ndjson.rs`, and the text writer into `crates/ro/src/render.rs`.

**Do not let "only 2 symbols are called" understate the live NDJSON surface — it is 9 call sites.**

## Test accounting

`ro-output` has **25 tests**. TOON kills 4; the dead `OutputFormat`/`parse_output_format`/`render` kill 5 more in `lib.rs`; `json.rs` kills 2; `format.rs` kills 6. **~17 die, ~5 survive** (the `ndjson.rs` ones). Carry the survivors into the new module.

## Text rendering — state it explicitly so nobody hunts for a renderer that does not exist

Text output is **hand-rolled `println!` per command handler**, which is what happens today. `--format text` stays the default; `json` and `ndjson` are the machine surfaces. **The plan does not build a shared text renderer.**

## Manifests — ro-output appears in FOUR places

Root `Cargo.toml` members, root `[workspace.dependencies]`, `crates/ro/Cargo.toml`, **and `crates/ro-sweep/Cargo.toml`**, which also depends on it. Missing any one is an immediate workspace-resolution error.
acceptance_criteria: ro-output crate deleted and removed from all four manifest sites. The 8 NdjsonEvent call sites compile against the new crates/ro/src/ndjson.rs. ~5 ndjson tests carried over. No shared text renderer was introduced.
close_reason: ro-output crate deleted in 9ccc22f; the 8 live NdjsonEvent constructors moved to crates/ro/src/ndjson.rs, covered by cli_ndjson.rs and the ndjson unit tests. TOON is gone from the tree.

title: Phase 3 — git, credential and safety substrate
description:
## Goal

Every primitive the fleet loop will call exists, the credential design is **buildable**, and nothing blocks forever.

## Why this phase is the one that makes or breaks the identity guarantees

The whole auth design rests on being able to (a) inject a credential into exactly one `git` invocation, (b) inject an author without touching the user's config, and (c) never let a process hang. None of the three is possible today:

- `run_in` has **no environment hook at all** — the credential design is literally uncompilable without changing its signature.
- `Command::output()` **blocks forever**, and `mutation.rs:17-18` explicitly defers timeout enforcement to "the daemon", which is being cut.
- `mutation::commit` **refuses an empty file list** and forbids `add -A`, so "commit everything" — the entire flagship use case — is impossible through the typed API. `ro-sweep/src/commit.rs:110-140` hand-rolls it in violation of ro-git's own rule.

## Scope

`run_in` gains `RunOpts`; a real timeout with child-kill; the missing git primitives; distinguishable errors; a relocated and non-TOCTOU `RepoLock`; the credential resolver; `AuthPolicy` in `ro-core`; `SecretString` with a non-leaking `Debug`; the extraheader push path; and the safety net actually wired.

## Done looks like

A hung git or a missing `gh` fails fast and per-repo, a token can be injected as a real credential, a paused rebase is detected, and the safety net actually blocks a secret.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads green. ro-git tests for stage_all in a brand-new untracked directory, create_branch, ahead_behind on a bad upstream, and conflict::detect on a paused rebase. A run_in test proves an injected env var reaches the child. An auth test proves GH_TOKEN wins over GITHUB_TOKEN. An unresolvable-credential test proves NO git push was attempted.
close_reason: Phase 3 complete. Children: ro-dab.1 (RunOpts), .2 (timeout + child-tree kill), .3 (primitives incl. stage_all), .4 (unknown vs in-sync), .5 (non-TOCTOU RepoLock), .6 (credential resolver), .7 (AuthPolicy/FailureClass in ro-core), .8 (SecretString), .9 (extraheader push), .10 (safety net). Also ro-ita.6 (write probe) and ro-pu9.7 (testkit) which the phase unblocked. Every claim verified by a negative control; see the individual commits.

title: run_in gains a RunOpts parameter — it must not lose the Option
description:
## The change

```rust
pub struct RunOpts<'a> {
    pub env: &'a [(String, String)],   // merged on top of the hardening block
    pub timeout: Option<Duration>,
}
fn run_in(cwd: Option<&Path>, args: &[&str], opts: &RunOpts<'_>) -> Result<GitCommandResult>;
```

## The detail that is easy to get catastrophically wrong

`run_in` is a **private** `fn run_in(cwd: Option<&Path>, args: &[&str])` at `crates/ro-git/src/mutation.rs:159`, and **the `Option` is load-bearing**: `clone()` calls it with `cwd: None` at `mutation.rs:262`, because git must run **outside** the destination repository.

An earlier draft of the plan proposed `run_in(repo: &Path, ...)`. That **deletes the only way to spawn git without a working directory** and breaks `clone()`. The correct change is to **add a third parameter**, keeping `Option<&Path>`.

## Keep the two-argument `run()` as a shim

Four non-test callers in `ro-sweep/src/commit_sweep.rs` (lines 204, 214, 436, 505) plus twelve test call sites would otherwise all churn for no benefit. Deprecate the shim; delete it when the sweep namespace goes in Phase 4.

## Preserve the arg-vector discipline exactly

`--` separators, **no shell interpolation**, `--no-pager`, and the hardening block (`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GCM_INTERACTIVE=Never`, `LC_ALL=C`, `GIT_PAGER=cat`). These are not incidental — they are what makes a git invocation safe to run from a config file and a diff.

## Why P0

Without this signature there is **no way to hand a credential to a single git invocation**, which makes the entire per-repo identity design unbuildable. Every later phase depends on it.

## Test

A `run_in` test proving an injected env var actually **reaches the child** — spawn something that prints its environment, or have a fake git shim echo it back. Asserting the `Command` was *built* with the variable is not enough; the failure mode being designed against is a variable that is set but never seen.
acceptance_criteria: run_in takes three parameters and keeps Option<&Path>. clone() still works. The two-arg run() shim exists and is deprecated. An injected env var is proven to reach the child process. Arg-vector discipline is unchanged.
close_reason: Landed. run_in takes RunOpts and keeps the optional cwd, because clone passes None and must run outside a destination that does not exist yet, and the reason is written on the parameter so a future tidy-up does not delete the only way to spawn with no working directory. The hardening block now wins over the caller environment, the opposite of my first attempt: my doc claimed the caller merged on top, the code let the caller win, and the test asserted only that brackets printed. All three were wrong together. Caller first then hardening last is the load-bearing order, because a caller that can set the terminal-prompt variable puts an interactive password prompt back on a command ro runs unattended, and the credential path is exactly where callers reach for env vars. Locale is in the same block because a caller-chosen locale changes how errors are phrased and the classifier matches English text. timeout is implemented here rather than deferred, because a field that does nothing is the same class of no-op Phase 1 called out as worse than an error; it kills and reaps the child, since a timeout that returns while the child lives on is worse than no timeout. The plan's shim story did not survive denied warnings: keeping run deprecated so sixteen call sites would not churn turns every one of them into a build error, so ro-sweep was migrated instead and the shim now has zero callers for Phase 4 to delete. The env tests run a real binary and read the value back from its own output, because asserting the command was built with the variable passes happily against the exact failure being designed against. Verified by dropping the env list and watching two tests fail, then restoring. 342 tests green, 5 new.

title: Wire the real safety net: secret scan, denylist, quality gates
description:
## The bug

The fleet path applies **only** the denylist. The `should_block(Warn, ...)` call at `ro-sweep/src/commit.rs:72` is **always false**, which makes the `BlockedBySecrets` variant **unreachable** — a repo containing a live-looking credential is not blocked, and the code that would have blocked it is dead.

The preflight runs before the engine, so this is the last thing standing between a WIP commit and a leaked credential.

## The fix

- Wire the real `SecretScanMode` (`off` / `warn` / `block`); `block` is the default in `[checkpoint]`.
- Report denylist hits as **warnings naming the file**, instead of dropping them silently. A silently skipped `.env` teaches the user that ro committed everything.
- `quality_gates` becomes **opt-in**, off by default, with the reason stated: `run_all` invokes `cargo test --workspace` over the **whole tree**, so an unrelated pre-existing failure in an untouched crate blocks a one-file commit, and across a twenty-repo fleet that check is the dominant cost of the run.
- Denylist as it stands: `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa`, `id_ed25519`, `**/.git/**`, `**/target/**`, `**/node_modules/**`.

## Carry `denylist.rs` and `secret_scan.rs` over **verbatim**

From Phase 4's move into `ro-engine` / staying in `ro-sweep`. Do not re-derive them; the existing implementation is correct apart from the unreachable branch.

## Tests

- A file containing a live-looking GitHub PAT **blocks** that repo and names the rule, **redacted** — the `should_block(Warn, ...)` regression.
- A dirty `.env` is excluded from the commit **and appears in the warnings output**.
- `quality_gates = "off"` by default: a repo with a failing suite still checkpoints. `"on"` blocks it.
- A brand-new directory with files inside is fully committed — the `-uall` behaviour, not `commit.rs:91`'s.
acceptance_criteria: A PAT-shaped file blocks the repo and the message is redacted. A .env is excluded AND warned about. quality_gates defaults off and on blocks. denylist and secret_scan are carried over unchanged apart from the reachable branch.
close_reason: Landed as ff403b2. The preflight called should_block(SecretScanMode::Warn, ...) which is always false - BlockedBySecrets was unreachable and a PAT-shaped file was committed. It was not a chosen value: the preflight had no configuration at all, so safety.secret_scan and review.quality_gates were validated and read by nobody. New [checkpoint] table carries both: secret_scan = block by default, naming the file and rule with the matched text redacted; quality_gates = off by default because run_all invokes cargo test --workspace over the whole tree, so an untouched pre-existing failure blocks a one-file commit. SweepSummary.gates_passed is now Option<bool> so a skipped gate is not reported as a pass. [review] removed with a deprecation note naming the new keys, since AppConfig has no deny_unknown_fields and the old table would be silently ignored. A block now exits non-zero. Verified end to end with the real binary in all three modes; the raw token never appears in output. Reintroducing the hardcoded Warn turns two tests red.

title: Give git commands a real timeout that kills the child tree
description:
## The problem

`Command::output()` **blocks forever**. `crates/ro-git/src/mutation.rs:17-18` explicitly defers timeout enforcement to "the daemon" — and the daemon is being cut.

So a hung SSH credential prompt, a network that never answers, or a remote that accepts the connection and stalls **currently stalls an entire fleet run indefinitely**. There is no cancellation and no recovery.

The declared `tokio` dependency has **zero references** — the crate is fully synchronous, so this is `std` work, not a runtime migration.

## The fix

- `RunOpts.timeout: Option<Duration>` (from the signature bead).
- Spawn, `try_wait` in a loop with a short sleep, and on expiry **kill the whole child tree** — on Windows via `taskkill /T /F /PID`, elsewhere via the process group.
- Return a distinguishable `TimedOut { after }`, **not** a generic `Failed`. A kill is not a refusal, and collapsing them means a hung credential and a bad flag produce the same message.
- The hardening block already sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GCM_INTERACTIVE=Never`, which prevents the most common interactive hang — the timeout is the backstop, not the mechanism.

## Test

A fake git that sleeps forever is killed at the timeout, the child tree is gone, and the result is `TimedOut` with the elapsed duration — **not** `Failed`. Without this, a single unreachable remote hangs the whole run and the user learns to kill the process rather than to use the tool.
acceptance_criteria: A hung git is killed at the timeout. The child process tree is gone. The outcome is TimedOut with a duration, distinct from Failed. No async runtime is introduced.
close_reason: Landed. RunOpts.timeout now spawns into a dedicated process group and signals the group, so the whole tree dies; Windows gets taskkill /T /F. A timeout that returns while its grandchildren live is worse than no timeout, because the fleet stalls anyway and now also reports success, and there is direct evidence: with the group signal replaced by a plain child kill the test run took 601 seconds instead of 1.8, because wait_with_output blocks on pipes a surviving grandchild holds open. The slowness is the bug. GitError makes TimedOut its own type with the duration and the args, not a string, because a kill is not a refusal and collapsing the two means a hung credential and a bad flag produce the same message, leaving the caller unable to tell try-again from this-will-never-work or from rate-limited. The tree kill is proved by a deferred side effect rather than by inspecting a pid, since checking a pid is racy across platforms and reports on liveness rather than on whether a survivor can still touch the worktree. The stale module doc deferring enforcement to a daemon that is being cut is corrected, and the tokio dependency this crate declared with zero references was already gone from the manifest. 358 tests green, 2 new.

title: Add the missing git primitives, including stage_all
description:
## Why

`mutation::commit` refuses an empty file list and **explicitly forbids `add -A`**. That is a good rule for a typed API in general and **the wrong rule for this tool** — WIP-style "commit everything" is the entire flagship use case. `ro-sweep/src/commit.rs:110-140` already hand-rolls it in violation of ro-git's own stated rule.

## Add

- `stage_all` — the `git add -A` path, with the `-uall` decision and the **nested-repo trailing-`/` guard** carried over verbatim from the existing sweep code
- `commit_all` — commit with a subject, no file list
- `create_branch`, `checkout`
- `diff` — worktree and staged separately
- `branch_exists`, `list_branches`
- `stash` — push and pop, for the autostash path
- standalone `merge` and `rebase` — `pull` currently conflates fetch+pull, and the rebase path needs to be a first-class operation with a distinguishable conflict outcome
- `remote_url`
- `git_config_user_email`

## The rebase outcome must be a value, not a bool

`PullOutcome::conflict` is computed and then discarded today, so a conflicted pull is recorded as `updated` / `success` / `error: None` — **a failed pull reported as a success**. The standalone `rebase` returns a real outcome the caller can branch on, which is what the `--resolve` stage in Phase 5 needs.

## Carry these over from ro-sweep verbatim, do not re-derive them

- the NUL-safe `parse_porcelain`
- the `-uall` decision plus the nested-repo trailing-`/` guard
- `is_protected_branch`

## Test

`stage_all` on a dirty repo containing a **brand-new untracked directory with files inside** produces one commit containing those files. That is the `-uall` behaviour, and `commit.rs:91`'s opposite is the bug being fixed.
acceptance_criteria: Every listed primitive exists with a test. stage_all commits a brand-new untracked directory's files in one commit. Standalone rebase returns a distinguishable conflict outcome. Porcelain parsing and the nested-repo guard are carried over unchanged.
close_reason: Landed as ro-git/src/primitives.rs: stage_all, commit_all, stage_paths, create_branch, checkout, current_branch, branch_exists, list_branches, diff_worktree, diff_staged, stash_push, stash_pop, merge, rebase, rebase_continue, rebase_abort, is_rebase_in_progress, conflicted_files, remote_url, git_config_user_email, ensure_repo, read_status, nested_or_dirs. parse_porcelain, is_protected_branch and the untracked-expansion decision are carried over verbatim from ro-sweep rather than re-derived, and nested_or_dirs is split out separately so the caller has to make the skip decision rather than it being folded into parsing. rebase returns MergeOutcome, a value and not a bool, separating Conflicted from Rejected because they exit non-zero identically and the caller has to tell resolve-this from this-will-never-work; a conflicted rebase is left mid-sequence on purpose since aborting discards the user's commits, and conflicted_files names the files the Phase 5 resolve stage has to edit. Three real bugs found by writing the tests rather than reading the code: a stash push without the include-untracked flag does not stash untracked files, so an autostash would have reported success while the operation it protected ran against a dirty tree with the newest files still in the way; the checkout separator has to go after the target rather than before, because in front of it the command means restore-this-path and fails with pathspec-did-not-match; and a plain diff shows only tracked files, so a diff test on a new file asserts nothing. The headline test commits a brand-new untracked directory with files at two depths and verifies by reading the committed tree rather than the worktree, because absence from the worktree is not presence in history and a hand-rolled find-the-dirty-files walk commits an empty tree here. 376 tests green, 18 new.

title: Make 'I do not know' distinguishable from 'you are in sync'
description:
## The bug

`crates/ro-git/src/read.rs:111-112` returns `AheadBehind::ZERO` on **any** git failure. That conflates *"I do not know"* with *"you are in sync"* — a **typo'd upstream displays as up to date**.

The same pattern appears twice more: `read::has_remote` and `read::merged_branches` swallow every error to a default, so **a broken repo is indistinguishable from a clean one**.

## Why it matters for a fleet tool

`ro list` and `ro status` walk twenty repos. A repo whose upstream is misconfigured, whose disk is failing, or whose `.git` is corrupt reports the same as a repo that is genuinely fine. The user sees a green fleet and does not know two of the twenty are unmeasured.

That is the same class of bug as the health-score cut: a number that is always zero when it cannot be computed is worse than no number.

## The fix

Distinguish the states. `ahead_behind` returns `Result<AheadBehind, GitError>` rather than a default. Callers surface an explicit `unknown` / `error` state per repo in the status line, and `ro doctor` reports which rows are unmeasurable.

## Test

`ahead_behind` against a typo'd upstream returns an **error**, not `AheadBehind::ZERO`. A corrupt `.git` produces a per-repo error line in `ro status`, not a clean row.
acceptance_criteria: ahead_behind returns Result. A bad upstream is an error. has_remote and merged_branches no longer swallow errors to a default. ro status shows an explicit unknown state for an unmeasurable repo.
close_reason: Landed as 8a54e48. ahead_behind, has_remote and remote_url all return Result; RepoStatus.ahead/behind are Option<u32> with unmeasurable_reason; is_in_sync() returns Option<bool>; ro status prints ahead=unknown behind=unknown. A repo with no origin stays in-sync (a fact), a repo whose remote lacks the tracked branch is unknown (a measurement that failed) - collapsing them would teach users to ignore the marker. One broken row no longer aborts the whole listing. Verified by reintroducing the original bug: exactly one test goes red. Also fixed the CI gate, red since earlier beads (deprecated shim call, unused import, dead method, two Debug-only structs).

title: Relocate RepoLock out of the worktree and close the TOCTOU
description:
## Two defects in `crates/ro-git/src/lock.rs`

**1. TOCTOU on drop.** `Drop` calls `remove_file(&self.lock_path)` at `lock.rs:84`. Process B can create the path after A's unlink and before A's unlock, and both then believe they hold the lock. **Fix: leave the file; only unlock.**

Fix A **breaks** the test `lock_acquire_and_release` (`lock.rs:95-105`), which asserts `!path.exists()` after drop. Update the test to assert the file's *contents* are unlocked, not that the file is gone.

**2. The lock makes the repo look dirty.** `acquire` writes `.ro.lock` **inside the worktree** and calls `create_dir_all(repo_path)`. Wired naively, `git status --porcelain` reports `?? .ro.lock`, `is_dirty` returns true, and checkpoint sees **its own lock as dirty work**.

**Fix: move the lock to `<state_dir>/locks/<hex>.lock`** and drop the `create_dir_all` side effect, so a typo'd path does not get created.

## The plumbing problem — the two fixes are individually correct but NOT composable as written

`RepoLock::acquire(repo_path, timeout_secs)` derives the path from `repo_path` and has **no `state_dir` parameter and no way to obtain one**. Forcing the relocation either adds a ro-git -> ro-config/ro-state edge — **inverting the current clean direction**, since ro-git currently depends on no workspace crate at all — or requires threading a new parameter through every caller.

Pick one deliberately and state it. The parameter is the smaller change; the edge inversion is not.

## Test

- A second acquire **succeeds** after the first is dropped (the TOCTOU fix).
- No `.ro.lock` appears in `git status --porcelain` after a run, and every repo reads as clean afterwards.
- A timeout'd acquire leaves no stray file.
acceptance_criteria: The lock lives under state_dir/locks, not in the worktree. Drop does not unlink. A second acquire succeeds after drop. No .ro.lock in git status. The state_dir plumbing is explicit.
close_reason: Landed. The lock moved from repo_path/.ro.lock to state_dir/locks/hash.lock, because inside the worktree it made status report the tool as dirty - a tool that dirties the tree it inspects cannot reliably inspect it. Drop no longer unlinks: the old code let process B create the path between A's unlink and A's unlock, and both then believed they held the lock while one worktree was mutated by both, so the lock became decorative exactly when two processes contended. Drop now only unlocks and the file survives holding nothing, which breaks lock_acquire_and_release - that test asserted the file was gone, pinning the bug, and now asserts the property the fix is for: a second acquire succeeds. On plumbing, took the parameter rather than the dependency edge: ro-git currently depends on no workspace crate and that is what makes it the leaf everything else points at, the same layering ro-dab.7 just consolidated, so inverting it to save one argument is a bad trade and a caller who forgets is now a compile error rather than a lock in the wrong tree. Also dropped create_dir_all on the repo path, so a typo no longer conjures a directory. The lock key canonicalizes first so a path and a symlink to it contend on one lock rather than two. Verified by putting the lock back in the worktree and watching two tests fail, then restoring. 345 tests green, 5 new.

title: Build the credential resolver: env: and keychain: references
description:
## The resolver

```
resolve_credential(repo) -> Result<SecretString, CredentialError>
  1. repos row's credential_ref, if non-NULL
  2. .ro/config.local.toml [auth] https/ssh, if the row is NULL
  3. [auth] from ~/.config/ro/config.toml
  4. none -> the machine's own credential (provider = Machine)
```

`env:<VAR>` reads that variable with **`var_os`, not `var`** — `var` fails on non-UTF8 values. `keychain:<name>` reads the OS keyring through the `keyring` crate, behind a **default-on `keychain` feature with an `env`-only fallback**, so a minimal build and a headless CI runner both still compile and work.

## The `keyring` crate is the ONE new runtime dependency in the whole plan

Everything else is in the workspace already.

## Rewrite `discover_token`

Today's chain is `GITHUB_TOKEN -> config token -> gh auth token` with every error swallowed (`ro-github/src/auth.rs:88-93`) — that is precisely the silent fallback the design forbids, and it is what ships today.

- `from_env` checks **`GH_TOKEN` first, then `GITHUB_TOKEN`**, matching gh CLI precedence. Today only `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read (`auth.rs:52`); `grep GH_TOKEN` over `crates/` returns **zero hits**.
- Delete the `auto` and `config-token` paths.
- Fix the GHE `/api/v3` base-URI suffix bug.
- `ro-github` re-exports the auth types from `ro-core` (see the next bead).

## Two CI properties this buys

- **No re-login, ever.** Switching a repo from a personal account to a work account is a one-word change in a file you already have open. No `gh auth login`, no `git config` edit, and no chance of the two drifting apart.
- **CI keeps working with no OS keychain.** `credential = "env:CI_GH_TOKEN"` is the answer on a headless runner. The keychain is the ergonomic default, **not a hard requirement** — a hard keychain requirement would make ro unusable in exactly the automation it is meant to help.

## Test

`credential = "env:CI_GH_TOKEN"` resolves from the environment. A `keychain:test-key` resolves through a `keyring` test backend. With the `keychain` feature disabled, the build still compiles and the error names the missing feature rather than failing to link.
acceptance_criteria: env: and keychain: both resolve. GH_TOKEN beats GITHUB_TOKEN. The keychain feature is default-on with an env-only fallback that compiles and works. The old swallowed-error chain is gone.

title: Define AuthPolicy, AuthProvider and FailureClass once in ro-core
description:
## The cycle an earlier draft created

The plan defined `AuthPolicy` in **two** places:
- `ro-config/src/resolve.rs::EffectiveConfig { pub auth: AuthPolicy }`
- `crates/ro-github/src/auth.rs`

and had ro-config read a type from ro-github. That requires **both** `ro-config -> ro-github` **and** `ro-github -> ro-config`, and `crates/ro-github/Cargo.toml` declares **no** ro-config dependency — its only workspace sibling is ro-core. The plan was simultaneously requiring two edges in opposite directions.

The same draft had `EngineOutcome::Failed { class: FailureClass }`, where `FailureClass` lives in `ro-jobs/src/failure.rs`, pulling a SQLite-shaped jobs crate into the engine layer purely to name an error discriminant — `ro-engine -> ro-jobs -> ro-state -> rusqlite`. A layering regression.

## The fix — ro-core, which is already a leaf

`ro-core` is depended on by ro-config, ro-github, and ro-sweep, and depends on nothing. Define once, there:

```rust
pub enum AuthProvider { Https, Ssh, Machine }

pub struct AuthPolicy {
    pub provider: AuthProvider,
    pub allow_fallback: bool,        // GLOBAL-ONLY — injected at the end
    pub expected_login: Option<String>,   // guard on the PUSHING account
    pub commit_identity: Option<CommitIdentity>,  // the author ro APPLIES
}

pub struct CommitIdentity { pub name: String, pub email: String }
pub enum FailureClass { /* one taxonomy, replacing two */ }
```

`ro-github` and `ro-jobs` **re-export** them for their existing APIs, so no caller has to churn at once. This kills both the cycle and the ro-engine -> ro-jobs edge in one move, and gives the identity guard a single home.

## The two identity fields are NOT the same thing

- `commit_identity` is the commit **author**, which ro **sets** (via `GIT_CONFIG_*`). It therefore cannot be wrong, so it needs no guard.
- `expected_login` is the **pushing** account, which is whatever the credential turns out to be and which ro does **not** control. That is what a guard is for.

Collapsing them produces a design where fixing your author silently starts author-guarding your push, or — worse — where a correct author suppresses a wrong-account push.

## `allow_fallback` is global-only

A per-repo fallback posture means one fleet run can hold **two** safety policies at once, and "which repo did we push as the wrong account?" then has no single answer afterwards. Resolve it from the global config and the `--allow-fallback` flag, then inject it into `AuthPolicy` at the end. A stale key in a per-repo file is a `deny_unknown_fields` error naming the right file.
acceptance_criteria: AuthPolicy, AuthProvider, CommitIdentity and FailureClass are defined once in ro-core. ro-github and ro-jobs re-export rather than redefine. Neither dependency cycle exists. commit_identity and expected_login are separate fields. allow_fallback is absent from RepoConfig and the per-repo file.
close_reason: Landed. AuthPolicy, AuthProvider, CommitIdentity and FailureClass are defined once in ro-core, which is already the leaf every dependent crate points at, and ro-jobs and ro-github re-export rather than redefine - so ro_jobs::FailureClass and ro_core::FailureClass are the same type. This kills the ro-config and ro-github mutual-dependency cycle in one move, and the ro-engine to ro-jobs edge along with it. commit_identity and expected_login are separate fields by design: the first is the commit author which ro sets and cannot get wrong, the second is the account the remote sees which ro does not control. allow_fallback is global-only so one fleet run cannot hold two safety policies at once. classify became FailureClass::classify(stderr) plus ro_jobs::classify_exit(exit_code, stderr), which consults the code first for 126 and 127 - could not execute, i.e. a missing binary, which a process that never started could not report in text. That makes MissingGit reachable for the first time, and fixes a stale doc reference to GitErrorKind that Phase 1 deleted. The layering is enforced by tests that parse the real manifests, not by a comment. Verified empirically rather than assumed: injected a ro-config to ro-github edge, confirmed the guard failed naming the offending edge, then restored and confirmed green. 309 tests green, 9 new.

title: SecretString whose Debug renders *** — the prerequisite for any token flowing anywhere
description:
## The bug

`crates/ro-github/src/auth.rs:10` has `AuthToken` deriving `Debug`. **`{:?}` prints the raw token.** `redact()` is opt-in and manual, and any `tracing` field, any `dbg!`, and any panic message that Debug-formats the token leaks it once tokens start flowing into child processes and argv.

This is a **prerequisite**, not a follow-up. It must land **before** the credential resolver and the extraheader push path, because both of those start putting a real secret into process arguments.

## The fix

- `SecretString` with a **manual** `Debug` that delegates to a single redaction rule and renders `***`.
- Delete the other two redaction implementations (Phase 1 consolidated the choice; this is where it is applied):
  - `ro_core::redaction::redact_secret` — 0 callers, and it byte-slices `&secret[..visible]` which **panics on a multi-byte boundary**
  - `ro_sweep::secret_scan::redact` — first-4, correct, but a second rule
- The identity guard needs **one** rule, not three.

## The transcript argument — why env injection is not a defence

Even with a perfect `Debug`, a secret handed to a subprocess can reach the agent's stdout, and an agent's transcript is **designed to be read and shared**. That is the opposite of a secret store. `SecretString` protects ro's own logs; it cannot protect a file ro does not write. The two defences together are: never put the secret where the agent can see it, and never let it print if something does.

## Tests

- A `tracing` field, a `dbg!`, and a `{:?}` on an error containing the credential all render `***`.
- A captured log line from a full run contains no value matching `ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}` or `github_pat_…`.
- `redact_secret` on a multi-byte secret does **not** panic.
acceptance_criteria: SecretString's Debug renders ***. Only one redaction rule exists in the tree. A captured log line from a full fleet run contains no PAT-shaped string. redact_secret does not panic on multi-byte input.
close_reason: Landed. SecretString in ro-core with a manual Debug rendering stars, and no Display at all - so format! with braces is a compile error rather than a silent redaction, and a caller wanting the value must write as_str, making every read greppable. The three disagreeing redaction rules are now one: the byte-slicing implementations that panicked on a multi-byte boundary are replaced by a chars-based one, and ro-github and ro-sweep both delegate to it. AuthToken wraps SecretString. Verified empirically rather than asserted: the first end-to-end check I wrote passed even after I deliberately broke Debug, because nothing in the tree Debug-formats a token - so it was a guard on the future that could not witness the present. It now says so in its own doc comment, and the check with teeth was added in ro-github asserting on Debug directly. Re-injecting the leak there made two tests fail with the leaked value printed; restoring made them pass. 323 tests green, 10 new.

title: Push with a per-invocation extraheader — the mechanism that works everywhere
description:
## The mechanism

```
git -c http.https://github.com/.extraheader="AUTHORIZATION: basic <base64(x-access-token:TOKEN)>" push
```

Per-invocation. **Nothing is persisted**, no global config is mutated, and the token exists only in the argv of the one git call that needs it.

## A claim in an earlier revision of the plan was WRONG — read this before implementing

The plan said *"`git` never reads `GH_TOKEN`, full stop"* and used that as the reason for the extraheader. The first half is true; **the conclusion drawn from it is not**, and on this machine it is false.

Verified with `credential.helper = manager` (Git Credential Manager, the default on a modern Windows and macOS install):

```
GH_TOKEN=ghp_MARKER   git credential fill  ->  username=x-access-token  password=ghp_MARKER
(no GH_TOKEN)         git credential fill  ->  username=qdang46          password=<keyring>
```

**GCM does read `GH_TOKEN` and will hand it to git.**

The accurate statement has three parts:

1. The `git` binary does not read `GH_TOKEN` — it asks a credential helper.
2. **Some helpers honour it** (GCM does). Others do not, and a user with `credential.helper=` cleared, or whose helper stores a different account, gets nothing.
3. **Therefore ro does not rely on it.** The extraheader is chosen precisely because it depends on **no helper being present at all**, applies to exactly one invocation, and never touches stored credentials.

## The failure mode this prevents — and it is the nastiest one

The same code **authenticates** on a machine with GCM and **silently falls through to the configured SSH key** on a machine without one. A test suite run on the first machine passes, and the tool ships broken on the second. It is a failure that looks like success.

**That is why the test asserts the header reached git, not that a push was attempted.** Every test of the form "a push was attempted" passes while the push went out over the wrong identity — which is the exact leak the whole design exists to prevent.

## Also rejected: `gh auth setup-git`

It **mutates the user's global git config**, permanently. A tool that rewrites global config to make its own authentication work leaves a mess when it is uninstalled, and it is a supply-chain surprise for anything else that reads that config.

## Tests

- The recorded git invocation carries the extraheader with the resolved credential.
- An unresolvable credential produces **no `git push` attempted at all** — assert the bare origin's reflog is unchanged.
- The same test on a machine with a credential helper configured and on one without produces the **same** result. This is the regression test for the corrected claim above.
acceptance_criteria: The push invocation carries the extraheader. No global git config is mutated. An unresolvable credential attempts no push. Behaviour is identical with and without a credential helper configured.
close_reason: Landed. push_with_credential attaches a per-invocation http extraheader through RunOpts env, so nothing is persisted and no global config is mutated. Environment rather than argv: the mechanism is identical either way, but argv is world-readable through ps on a shared machine and a tool whose premise is that a credential in the wrong place leaks should not be the one putting it there. The corrected claim is now a test: Git Credential Manager reads GH_TOKEN and hands it to git, a machine without a configured helper gets nothing from the same code and falls through to the SSH key, so the identical tool authenticates on one machine and pushes as somebody else on the other while a suite run on the first passes - the header is asserted identical with and without a helper configured. The test took three attempts and the record matters: the first assembled the environment by hand and proved only that the builder was correct, so dropping the env inside push_with_credential left it green. The second put a shim on PATH, which is process-global and made every other test in the binary racy, with a panic between swap and restore leaving the shim in place and twelve unrelated assertions failing. The third names the shim through a new RunOpts.program, so the environment is never touched - a field that is not test-only, since a caller needing a credential broker, a sandboxed binary, or a recorded run has no other way to say so. What is asserted is what the child received, not that a push was attempted, because a push attempt succeeds over the wrong identity. Also covered: no credential means no header rather than an empty one, and an unresolvable credential leaves the bare origin reflog untouched. Verified by dropping the env and watching three tests fail with the empty header printed. 352 tests green, 8 new.

title: Phase 2 — registry and global config
description:
## Goal

The registry verbs exist and work, per-repo settings live in the registry, and `ro doctor` can tell you **which repos it will not be able to push to** before you run anything.

## Why this phase

Three of the plan's load-bearing decisions land here: the per-repo config is a **row in SQLite** rather than a file; the credential is a **reference** rather than a value; and doctor checks **write access** rather than token presence. Each one has a failure mode that is invisible until it is expensive.

## Scope

- **V5** adds four columns to `repos`: `credential_ref`, `author_ref`, `engine`, `engine_args`.
- `ro add` accepts a local path as well as a remote spec, with structural disambiguation.
- The `RepoSpec` drive-letter bug is fixed in `ro-core`.
- `ro config set` gains the registry tier and stops destroying the config file.
- A credential value that is not a reference is a **loud error at write time**.
- `ro doctor` gains the per-remote write-access probe.
- `ro init` stays deliberately dumb.
- A `[providers]` compat shim so existing configs do not silently lose their engine.

## Done looks like

`ro add`, `ro list`, `ro remove` and `ro doctor` do what they say; a per-repo engine, credential and author can be set without a text editor; and doctor tells you before a run which repos are going to fail.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads green. V5 applied twice in a row without error. A pasted token is refused with a message naming the two accepted forms. ro doctor reports write: NO for a read-only credential and write: yes for a writable one, with the fake remote recording ZERO writes.
close_reason: Phase 2 complete. Six of seven children landed: V5 with the four per-repo config columns and a Guarded migration variant, RepoSpec rejecting a Windows path in ro-core so every caller inherits the fix, credential references that make a pasted token a parse error in three places, ro add taking a local path or a remote spec told apart structurally, ro config set editing the document instead of re-encoding a struct, and the providers compat shim. The seventh, ro-ita.6, needed a credential resolver from Phase 3 and landed after it. The tree is a registry and a global config with no per-repo file, no token in any layer, and no fleet run that can be surprised by an account nobody chose.

title: Add V5: credential_ref, author_ref, engine, engine_args on repos
description:
## The migration

```sql
-- V5_ADD_REPO_CONFIG
ALTER TABLE repos ADD COLUMN credential_ref TEXT;   -- NULL | 'env:VAR' | 'keychain:name'
ALTER TABLE repos ADD COLUMN author_ref     TEXT;   -- NULL = [identity].default
ALTER TABLE repos ADD COLUMN engine        TEXT;   -- NULL = use [agent] engine
ALTER TABLE repos ADD COLUMN engine_args   TEXT;   -- NULL = use [agent] command
```

These four columns are the **entire** per-repo config layer.

## Trap 1 — ADD COLUMN is NOT idempotent in SQLite

Re-running it on a migrated database errors with `duplicate column name`. Guard it the way the existing `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` migrations are guarded, or **the second run of ro on an upgraded machine fails at open**. This is the single most likely way a migration like this ships broken.

## Trap 2 — anything that enumerates columns by hand must be updated in the SAME commit

- `manage::add` inserts a **fixed column list** (`ro-state/src/migrate.rs:331,337`)
- `manage::list` selects a `REPO_COLUMNS` **constant**

A stale enumeration returns rows whose new columns are `None` while ro believes the repo is configured — a silent wrong answer, not a compile error.

## Why `author_ref` and not the email on the row

The same reason credentials are references. Two rows for the same person drift, an email change becomes a migration, and the row carries the only piece of personal data in a database that gets backed up and pasted into issues. Instead:

```toml
[identity]
default = "personal"
[identity.work]
name  = "Dang Tran Quang"
email = "quang@company.com"
[identity.personal]
name  = "Dang Tran Quang"
email = "me@gmail.com"
```

The row names a **profile**, not an address.

## This fixed a real regression in the plan

Removing `ro.local.toml` removed the only per-repo author override, while a test still asserted that two repos in one run commit as two different people. **A test that cannot fail is worse than no test.** `author_ref` restores the capability and the test now exercises a column that exists.

## Tests

- V5 applied twice in a row without error (the idempotency guard).
- V5 applied to a **pre-V5 database that already has rows** leaves every existing row with `credential_ref IS NULL` and `author_ref IS NULL` — i.e. every existing repo keeps the global credential, which is the correct back-compat behaviour and not merely the absence of a migration.
- `ro config set repos.cass.engine = codex` then `ro list` shows `codex` for cass and the global engine for every other row.
- A `SELECT` that enumerated `repos` columns before V5 does not silently return nulls for the new columns.
acceptance_criteria: Four columns exist. V5 is idempotent. A pre-V5 database upgrades with every row on the global credential. A per-repo engine set on one row does not affect another.
close_reason: Landed in one commit, both halves. Migration: Migration::Guarded variant, because SQLite has no ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS and a replay after a crash between the ALTER and the _meta write would otherwise kill ro at open with 'duplicate column name'. column_exists moved to production on PRAGMA table_info - the old test-local SELECT-col-LIMIT-1 trick is wrong on an empty table. Enumeration: REPO_COLUMNS, row_to_tracked, and add all updated together, with the INSERT deliberately naming no config columns so an omitted column takes its default. Five new tests: the v4->v5 upgrade on a populated database leaving every column NULL, V5 invoked twice at the same version (the version gate would skip it, so the step is called directly to prove it is re-runnable alone), the four columns surviving a list round trip, per-row isolation, and a fresh row inheriting. 261 tests green, clippy and fmt clean.

title: Fix RepoSpec so a Windows path cannot parse as a repo spec
description:
## The bug

`ro add C:/work/backend` **succeeds** and inserts a garbage row.

`crates/ro-core/src/repo_spec.rs` splits on `/` and requires two parts. `C:/work/backend` splitn(2, '/') gives `["C:", "work/backend"]` — length 2, passes. The result:

```
owner     = "C:"
name      = "work/backend"
clone_url = "https://github.com/C:/work/backend.git"
```

A row for an owner that does not exist, failing much later as a clone error against a nonsense URL.

Note `ro add .` and `ro add C:\work\backend` already fail **correctly** — they have no `/`, so the two-part split rejects them. The forward-slash form is the hole.

## Fix it in ro-core, not in the handler

In `RepoSpec::parse` (`repo_spec.rs:34-108`):
1. Reject a `owner` matching `^[A-Za-z]:$` — a Windows drive letter.
2. Reject any spec containing a **backslash**.

Fixing it in the `ro add` handler means every other caller of `RepoSpec::parse` keeps the bug. There is exactly one caller today, and there will be more.

## Two test cases, three lines of code

- `RepoSpec::parse("C:/work/backend")` is an error
- `RepoSpec::parse("C:\\work\\backend")` is an error (**already true** — no `/` — but assert it so the drive-letter fix does not regress it)

This is the smallest bug on the list and the cheapest to leave open: nothing finds it until a user on Windows types a path.
acceptance_criteria: Both Windows path forms are rejected by RepoSpec::parse. A bare owner/repo still parses. No handler-local special case exists — the fix is in ro-core.
close_reason: Fixed in ro-core, not the handler, so every RepoSpec::parse caller inherits it. Two checks for two different failure modes: a backslash is rejected in parse up front (the backslash form already failed, but on the two-part split, which gave a misleading message), and a drive letter is rejected in from_host_owner_name where the owner is actually extracted - that is the path every host-prefixed form routes through, and it is where a drive check can be made without false-positiving on a real owner. Three new tests: the forward-slash Windows path, the backslash one, and the drive-letter predicate against real one- and two-character owners.

title: ro add accepts a local path or a remote spec, disambiguated structurally
description:
## Two inputs, one verb, and the disambiguation is structural — not a guess

```bash
ro add git@github.com:quangdang46/cass.git    # remote spec -> clone, then register
ro add .                                        # local path -> adopt in place
```

The rule, in order:
1. A value carrying a recognised host prefix (`github.com/`, `https://`, `git@`) parses as a **remote spec**.
2. Anything else resolving to a directory containing `.git` is a **local path**.
3. Anything else is refused with a message naming **both** accepted forms.

This ordering matters: the spec branch runs first so a URL is never mistaken for a path, and the path branch never attempts to parse a local directory as a GitHub coordinate.

## Flags

```
--name <ALIAS>       display and lookup alias
--tag <T>            repeatable; writes repo_tags
--clone-to <DIR>     where a URL clone lands
--branch <B>         clone -b <B>. A CLONE PARAMETER, not a config cache.
--credential <REF>   per-repo credential reference
--engine <NAME>      per-repo engine for this row
--author <PROFILE>   which [identity.*] profile commits this repo
```

**`--branch` is a clone parameter with no lifetime**, not a cached default branch. A `repos.default_branch` column was **dropped in V4** precisely because a cache of a branch name goes stale on a rename; re-adding it to hold a value git can be asked is the drift the plan spent two rounds removing.

## Cloning is all-or-nothing per repo

A failed clone writes **no row**. This is what makes "tracked but not cloned" a state the system never enters, rather than one it has to tolerate in four places.

## Tests

- `ro add` on an unreachable remote clones nothing and writes **no** row (assert the `repos` table count is unchanged).
- `ro add <local path>` with no `.git` is refused, naming both accepted forms.
- `--tag` writes real `repo_tags` rows; tagging twice is a no-op at exit 0.
- `--name` sets the alias and the repo resolves by it afterwards.
acceptance_criteria: Both input forms work. A failed clone writes no row. A value matching neither form is refused naming both. --branch is passed to clone -b and nothing is persisted.
close_reason: Landed. classify_add_input checks a recognised host prefix first so a URL is never probed on the filesystem, then falls to resolves-to-a-directory-containing-dot-git, then refuses by name listing both accepted forms. Local paths are canonicalized on the way in so the stored local_path compares equal to what the orphan walker produces later. Building it caught a real hole: ro_git mutation clone reports a non-zero git exit inside the outcome rather than as an Err, so the first version registered a repo after a clone that had failed outright. Without checking outcome.result.ok, tracked-but-not-cloned is a state the system manufactures rather than tolerates. A failed clone also removes the half-written directory. Credential validation now runs ahead of the clone. The branch flag is a clone parameter and is deliberately not cached on the row, because V4 dropped repos.default_branch since a branch-name cache goes stale on a rename. Added ro_git read remote_url, which the per-repo clone_url needs. Nine new tests, 280 green.

title: ro config set writes surgically with toml_edit and gains the registry tier
description:
## The repair — today it destroys the file on every call

`ro config set` loads, mutates one of seven hardcoded keys, re-validates, and `fs::write`s the whole `AppConfig`. That **silently drops every comment and every key the schema does not model, on every invocation**.

Use **`toml_edit` for a surgical in-place edit.** That fixes the loss structurally, which means **do not also write a `.bak` per call** — a backup accumulated on every key assignment is noise, and it does not fix the loss anyway. A `.bak` belongs on the one genuinely destructive operation (the V4/V5 migrations), not on every assignment.

## The addition — the registry tier

```bash
ro config set repos.cass.engine          = codex
ro config set repos.cass.credential_ref  = keychain:gh-personal
ro config set repos.cass.author_ref      = personal
```

This is how most per-repo changes should be made: it is **queryable, diffable in a backup, and does not litter working trees**. The `.ro/config.local.toml` file is for the cases where the registry is not yours to change — someone else's machine, a repo you are debugging by hand, a setting that must not persist in your `state.db`.

## The five-layer precedence this feeds

```
CLI flag  >  .ro/config.local.toml  >  repos row  >  ~/.config/ro/config.toml  >  defaults
```

**The file wins over the registry, unconditionally**, and `ro doctor` reports when a repo has the same key in both places with different values. Silent divergence between two sources of truth is worse than either source alone, so the disagreement is made loud rather than resolved by convention.

## ro doctor --fix must be able to UPGRADE an existing config

`check_and_optionally_fix_config` writes `default_config_toml()` only when the file is **absent**. After this phase rewrites the defaults, every existing user keeps dead `[mcp]`/`[jobs]`/`[review]` config indefinitely and `validate()` keeps checking keys the schema no longer models.

With `toml_edit` available, `--fix` should add the missing `[identity]`/`[auth]`/`[agent]`/`[checkpoint]` sections, **leave unknown legacy tables in place** (deleting a user's file contents is not a repair), and print a note naming the sections it is ignoring.

Two related defects to fix while you are in the file: `doctor.rs:200` discards the applied-fix count via `let _ = applied_fix_count;`, and the module doc's claim that every mutation "backs up the prior state to `<state_dir>/doctor/runs/<run-id>/`" is **false** — no backup code exists. Delete the claim.

## Tests

- A hand-written comment survives `ro config set`.
- An unmodelled key survives `ro config set`.
- No `.bak` is written on a normal set.
- `ro config set repos.<name>.<key>` writes the registry and the file is untouched.
- `ro doctor --fix` on a legacy config adds the new sections and **leaves** the legacy ones, printing what it ignored.
acceptance_criteria: Comments and unmodelled keys survive a config set. No per-call .bak. The registry tier writes and reads. doctor --fix upgrades an existing config without deleting unknown tables.
close_reason: Landed. set_key_in_file edits the parsed toml_edit document instead of re-encoding AppConfig, so comments and unmodelled tables survive an assignment. The edit is validated before it is kept and a rejected edit leaves the original bytes alone - a config that no longer parses is worse than one with the old value, and there is no backup to reach for, which is also why no .bak is written. The validation reason is folded into the message rather than attached as a context layer, because a user who typed a bad value needs to be told what was wrong right there. Registry tier added: ro config set repos.NAME.KEY routes through the existing manage::set_repo_config, so the credential validation from ro-ita.5 applies with no second copy of the rule. Both doctor.rs defects fixed: the applied_fix_count that was computed, named, then dropped as reserved-for-future-scoring is now reported, and the module doc claim that every mutation backed up prior state to doctor/runs/RUN-ID is deleted since no such code existed. --fix now upgrades an existing config by adding the sections it predates, which it never did before; it adds and never removes, leaves legacy tables in place, and names them in the output so a table ro ignores is visible rather than merely tolerated. Building it caught a regression: ro add acme/api broke because the bare owner/repo form was not in the host-prefix list and got refused, breaking two integration tests. It is now the third branch of classify_add_input, after host prefix and after is-this-a-directory-with-dot-git, last of the three because it is the only remote form a real directory can also match. 295 tests green, 15 new.

title: A credential that is not a reference is a loud error at write time
description:
## The rule

In **every layer** — global TOML, the `repos` row, and `.ro/config.local.toml` — a credential is a **reference**, never a value.

```
https = "env:GH_PERSONAL_TOKEN"     the variable to read
https = "keychain:gh-personal"      the keyring entry to read
```

A key named `token` with a value does not parse. `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` turns a pasted `ghp_...` into a **loud error at write time** with a message naming the two accepted forms.

## Why this is P0 and not a style rule

`state.db` is **backed up, synced, and pasted into issues**. `config.toml` is committed-adjacent and lives in a working directory. The agent's transcript is a file ro does not write but the engine's process can read. A live credential in any of those is a credential in every one of those places.

The same reasoning applies to `[identity]`: the row holds `author_ref`, a **name**, not an address.

## What the resolver does at push time

```
resolve_credential(repo_root) -> Result<SecretString, CredentialError>
  1. the repo row's credential_ref, if non-NULL
  2. .ro/config.local.toml's [auth] https, if the row is NULL
  3. [auth] https from the global config
  4. none -> the machine's own credential (SSH agent, git credential manager, gh)
```

The resolved secret is wrapped in a `SecretString` whose `Debug` renders `***`.

## `env:` and a bare `GH_TOKEN` are not the same thing

`env:WORK_GH_TOKEN` names a **specific** variable for a **specific** repo, so one fleet run can push repo A with a work token and repo B with a personal one in the same process. A bare `GH_TOKEN` is one value for the whole environment, which is exactly the "one account for everything" problem per-repo config exists to solve.

## Tests

- A pasted `ghp_...` is **rejected** in the global config, in the registry, and in the per-repo file — three separate paths, three tests.
- `credential_ref = 'env:CI_GH_TOKEN'` resolves **only** that variable; setting `GH_TOKEN` to a different value does not change which credential is used.
- A repo row with `credential_ref = 'env:WORK'` and another with `'env:PERSONAL'` push with **two different accounts in one run**.
- `env:` naming a variable that is not set fails that repo with a message naming the variable. It does **not** fall through to `GH_TOKEN`.
acceptance_criteria: A token value is an error in all three layers. env: references are repo-precise. Two repos with different env references push as different accounts in one run. An unset variable fails that repo without falling back.
close_reason: Landed. CredentialRef in ro-core has no public constructor that skips validation, so a value in hand is proof it was checked. Three rejection paths: the global config via serde(deny_unknown_fields) on the new [auth] table (which is what makes token = "ghp_..." an error rather than silently ignored), the value itself via Deserialize, and the registry row via manage::set_repo_config, which parses before the UPDATE so a rejected write leaves the row untouched. Registry validation deliberately lives in ro-sync rather than in ro config set, because credential_ref is the one column whose meaning is 'the thing ro reads instead of asking for a token' - every writer needs the check including a future one - and the four keys carry an is_credential_reference flag so the call site has one rule. env: with an empty name is rejected: it would otherwise resolve to nothing and fall through to the machine's own credential, a silent fallback the design forbids more emphatically than a wrong credential. Third path (the .ro/config.local.toml per-repo file) is not applicable yet - that file does not exist; it lands with the precedence work. 276 tests green, 15 new. ro-config depends on ro-core again; Phase 1 removed that edge as unused and it now has a caller.

title: ro doctor checks write access per remote, not just token presence
description:
## The check that actually prevents a failed run

Today `ro doctor` verifies that **a** GitHub token exists. That is the check that lets a wrong-account situation straight through.

What prevents a failed run is: **can this repo's credential write to this repo's remote?** A token with `repo` scope and no write access on one repository is an entirely ordinary state.

It is the state **this repository was in when the plan was written**: `qdang46` authenticated, `quangdang46/repo_orchestrator` remote, `push: false` — discovered only at the push step, as a 403, after four other repos had already been pushed.

```
✓ git                    2.45.0
✓ gh                     2.89.0
✓ claude                 /usr/local/bin/claude
✓ codex                  not installed            (informational — not a default)

repos:
  ✓ voice-ai-dashboard    company  (me@corp.com)     write: yes
  ✗ cass                 personal (me@gmail.com)   write: NO   <- 403, push will fail
```

That last line is the entire point of the check: a 403 discovered **after** a fleet run has pushed to four repos becomes a warning discovered **before** any of them were touched.

## The probe must READ the permission, never exercise it

A doctor that writes to prove it can write is a doctor that mutates state. `GET .../repos/{owner}/{repo}` returns a `permissions` object; read `push` from it. The fake remote must record **zero** writes.

## Also in this bead: `.ro/config.local.toml` versus the registry

`ro doctor` reports when a repo sets the same key in both places **with different values**, and names the file it found. Silent divergence between two sources of truth is worse than either alone.

## Do NOT add engine-availability probes here

An earlier revision of the plan contradicted itself — saying availability is checked at dispatch only, then adding a `gh` probe to doctor. **Do not add probes.** `check_provider` is already `Severity::Optional` (`doctor.rs:372`), so it can only ever warn and cannot change `DoctorReport::exit_code()`. Say that in the docs. Two existing tests need comment updates, not behaviour changes: `doctor.rs:562` `run_returns_at_least_six_checks` asserts `>= 6` (still true) and `doctor.rs:536` asserts `Severity::Optional` (still true).

## Tests

- A credential that authenticates but lacks write permission reports `write: NO` and **the fake remote records zero writes**.
- A valid credential reports `write: yes`, also with zero writes.
- An unresolvable credential is reported **distinctly** from a resolved-but-forbidden one. They look identical to a user — the push does not work — and they have completely different fixes.
- Doctor on a registry with one broken remote exits non-zero and **still prints the healthy rows**. A doctor that stops at the first failure tells the user one thing when there are three.
acceptance_criteria: doctor reports write: yes / write: NO per remote with the account it resolved to. The probe performs zero writes. Unresolvable and forbidden are distinct. One broken row does not suppress the others.
close_reason: Landed. ro doctor reports write yes or NO per remote with the account the credential resolved to, one CheckResult per repo so one broken row does not suppress the others, and exits 1 when any row is broken. WriteAccess is an enum rather than a bool because unresolvable and forbidden both make a push fail and are fixed by opposite actions; the login is read before the repository, which is what makes the two distinguishable at all. The probe READS - GET /user then GET /repos/owner/name - and the fake GitHub records every request with the tests asserting zero non-GETs.
